title: How to Fix a Broken Table of Contents in Kindle Books
excerpt: A broken table of contents is one of the most common reasons KDP flags a Kindle book. Here is what causes it and how to fix the TOC so navigation works on every device.
meta_title: How to Fix a Broken Table of Contents in Kindle Books | BookKraft AI
meta_description: Kindle table of contents not working? Learn what breaks a Kindle TOC and how to rebuild it with real headings and a valid NCX so navigation works on every device.
feature_image_alt: An author checking the table of contents of an ebook on a Kindle device
html:
You upload your book to KDP and get a warning: the table of contents can't be found, or it points to the wrong chapters. Sometimes the book still goes live, and a reader complains that the Go To menu jumps them to the middle of chapter four. A broken table of contents is one of the most common Kindle formatting problems, and it almost always comes from the same handful of causes.

The good news: you can fix it yourself without touching raw code, and this guide walks through each cause in order.

How a Kindle table of contents actually works

A Kindle book has two separate tables of contents, and they do different jobs. The first is the inline TOC — the clickable list of chapters that appears as a page near the front of the book. The second is the navigation TOC, stored in a file called the NCX (and, for EPUB 3, a nav.xhtml document). This is what powers the Go To menu and the progress bar on the device itself.

When people say their Kindle TOC is "broken," they usually mean the navigation TOC is missing or pointing at the wrong anchors. Both need to exist, and both need to agree with each other.

1. Chapter titles are styled by hand, not as headings

This is the number one cause. If you made your chapter titles big and bold in Word instead of applying the Heading 1 style, the Kindle has no way to know they are chapters. It can't build a navigation TOC from text that only looks like a heading.

Fix: Apply Heading 1 to every chapter title and Heading 2 to sub-sections. Change how the heading looks by editing the style itself, never by formatting the text directly. Once your headings are real headings, most conversion tools will build a correct navigation TOC automatically. Our free TOC Generator builds a clean, linked contents page from your heading structure.

2. The NCX file is missing or out of date

If you reordered or renamed chapters after your first export, the NCX can end up pointing at anchors that no longer exist. KDP reads the NCX to build the in-reader menu, so stale navPoints send readers to the wrong place. A missing NCX triggers the well-known "No TOC Found" warning at upload.

Fix: Regenerate the file so the navigation TOC is rebuilt from your current chapters. If you are working inside the EPUB, confirm the NCX is listed in the OPF manifest and that every navPoint references a real chapter file. Our guide to the "No TOC Found" error covers this step by step.

3. The inline TOC links point at page numbers

Page numbers don't exist in a reflowable Kindle book. If your inline contents page links to page numbers instead of chapter bookmarks, tapping an entry does nothing.

Fix: Every inline TOC entry must be a hyperlink to a bookmark or heading anchor, not a page reference. Rebuild the contents page so each line links directly to its chapter heading.

4. Duplicate or broken anchors inside the file

EPUB requires every id attribute to be unique across the whole book. When a converter copies the same heading id into every chapter, the navigation links collide and resolve to the wrong target. This also causes EPUBCheck errors that can block Apple Books submission.

Fix: Run the file through a validator to surface duplicate ids and broken references. The free BookKraft AI EPUB Validator lists them in plain language so you know exactly which anchors to repair. For the underlying error, see our reference on missing NCX navigation.

Verify the fix before you upload

Once you have rebuilt the TOC, confirm it works:

  1. Validate the file with the EPUB Validator to clear structural errors and duplicate anchors.
  2. Open Kindle Previewer, tap Go To, and check that every chapter jumps to the right place.
  3. Test the inline contents page by tapping each entry — every link should land on its chapter heading.

A table of contents that passes all three checks will navigate correctly on Kindle e-readers, phones, and tablets. If you would rather not chase this by hand, the TOC Generator and EPUB Validator together handle both halves of the problem — building the contents and confirming it resolves.
